gaps.explanation: Re-read pp8-11 (governmental funds statement, printed pp21-24), p16-17 (proprietary statement, printed pp29-30), pp20-21 (budget schedule, printed pp48-49), p22 (schedule of expenditures, printed p51). Revenue detail was only the combined all-funds 'Budgetary Comparison Schedule - Cash Basis - Total Primary Government' (p20, unaudited), fund 'Total Primary Government': its governmental-tagged lines (indices 0-9) total 365,926, and the governmental receipts Franchise 3,483, Occupation 4,110, Carline 430, Charges for services 13,108, Lease fees/rentals 16,622, Fees/permits/licenses 1,004, Interest 27, Donations 5,380, Park Fund Grants 16,500, Sale of assets 13,765, Insurance proceeds 58,847, Other revenues 7,837 (= 141,113 = gap) sit inside the single mixed line 'Local Receipts: Other' 1,327,744 (index 10, tagged business-type, no printed breakdown). The statement p8-9 prints every governmental row per fund column (General 180,604, Street and Alley 163,591, City Hall 41,912, Park 90,108, Pool 30,824, Grants 0; Total 507,039). Per the per-fund rule (cities and villages: a combined all-funds schedule is replaced by one line per fund column), the 62 non-zero fund-column cells are added and the combined budget revenue lines, which hold the same money, are removed (indices 0-9 here; index 10 under the business-type revenue entry). Each added column re-adds to its printed Total Revenue; rows re-add to the printed Total column (e.g. Property 7,139 + 46,313 + 5,885 + 23,113 + 7,131 = 89,581). Result: 365,926 - 365,926 + 507,039 = 507,039 = statement.

gaps.explanation: Detail transfers in 172,754 = combined all-funds budget line 'Transfers' 109,502 (index 11, p20, fund 'Total Primary Government', tagged governmental) + per-fund statement lines General 6,000 and Street and Alley 57,252 (p10, already in detail). The same transfers are also in detail per fund on the business side (p17: Sewer 33,550, Water 3,800, Trash 3,800 in). The combined line counts the same money a second time (fund-column transfers in 63,252 + 41,150 = 104,402; the unaudited cash-basis budget prints 5,100 more, no breakdown) - removed; the printed fund-column lines hold the money. Remaining: 63,252 vs statement Total 4,800 = the printed Adjustments column (58,452) on p11 that nets the governmental interfund transfers (gross per fund vs netted Total, both printed); no line to add.

Detail holds the printed fund-column transfers out General (77,002) and Street and Alley (2,700) (p10) = 79,702; statement Total (21,250) on p11 is after the printed Adjustments column 58,452. 79,702 - 58,452 = 21,250. Gross per fund vs netted Total, both printed; nothing missing or duplicated.

The only business-type revenue detail line was the combined budget line 'Local Receipts: Other' 1,327,744 (index 10, p20, fund 'Total Primary Government', cash basis, unaudited), which mixes governmental receipts (141,113, now in detail per governmental fund column, see the governmental revenue entry) and utility receipts with no printed breakdown. Per the per-fund rule it is replaced by one line per printed row per enterprise fund column of the proprietary statement p16 (never the Totals column): Electric 673,387 + 10,569 + 3,850 + 2,833 + 11,472 + 2,514 + 2,047 = 706,672; Sewer 102,349 + 31 + 6,055 + 2,491 = 110,926; Water 113,197 + 550 + 27 + 11,472 + 2,183 + 127 = 127,556; Trash 81,172 + 600 + 47,293 + 756 = 129,821; sum 1,074,975 = statement (operating 985,674 + nonoperating revenues 89,301). The cash-basis budget figure also held Trash loan proceeds 116,007 printed only on the cash flow statement (p18), which by rule are not added.

gaps.explanation: Business-type spending detail is the budget schedule's per-fund lines (p21, cash basis, unaudited, heading 'Disbursements and Transfers'): Electric 797,927, Trash 247,180, Sewer 142,497, Water 128,819 = 1,316,423 (indices 12-15). These are printed per-fund lines, not a combined all-funds line, so they are kept. Statement 1,003,344 = proprietary p16 operating expenses 981,428 + interest expense 21,916 (accrual, incl. depreciation 114,246). Per fund (budget - statement): Electric 797,927 - 673,879 = +124,048; Sewer 142,497 - (97,934 + 13,264) = +31,299; Water 128,819 - (110,887 + 4,866) = +13,066; Trash 247,180 - (98,728 + 3,786) = +144,666; total 313,079 = -gap. The cash budget includes capital purchases (331,589) and debt principal (80,000) printed on the cash flow statement p18, excludes depreciation, and by its heading may include Electric's transfer out (24,700, which detail also holds from p17); no breakdown is printed, so nothing can be split or removed without a derived figure.
